encounters.cc: Feeling anxious, warm, and 'on edge' for the past four days with palpitations and difficulty sleeping

lines: Feeling anxious, warm, and 'on edge' for the past four days with palpitations and difficulty sleeping
She reports frequent palpitations, difficulty sleeping, and excessive sweating, despite a normal environment.
Her appetite has increased slightly, but she has not noticed significant weight changes.
She gave birth to her first child eight weeks ago following an uncomplicated full-term pregnancy and vaginal delivery.
She has no family history of thyroid disease
She denies sore throat, recent illness
Her temperature is 98.6°F, pulse is 112/min, and blood pressure is 120/76 mm Hg.
On exam, she has fine tremor of the hands but no thyroid tenderness, enlargement, or eye changes.
A radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan and laboratory studies are performed.

encounters.cc: Pain and swelling in left breast with fatigue and chills

lines: Pain and swelling in left breast with fatigue and chills

The patient is a 33-year-old female with a history of postpartum depression and postpartum thyroiditis seen in Endocrinology in 2020, presenting with a 2-day history of pain and swelling in her left breast.
She delivered a healthy newborn via spontaneous vaginal delivery 2 weeks ago and has been breastfeeding exclusively.
She reports fatigue, chills, and difficulty nursing on the affected side due to pain.
The infant has recently started biting during feeding.
On examination, the upper outer quadrant of the left breast is erythematous, warm, indurated, and tender to palpation.
A fissure is present on the left nipple.
There is no fluctuance or drainage.

encounters.cc: Six-week postpartum check-up with concerns about relationship stress

lines: Six-week postpartum check-up with concerns about relationship stress

The patient is a 33-year-old female with a history of postpartum depression and postpartum thyroiditis and recent treatment for lactational mastitis who returns for her six-week postpartum visit following an uncomplicated vaginal delivery.
She reports feeling overwhelmed with caring for her newborn and expresses concern about her relationship with her partner, noting that they have been arguing more frequently.
She mentions that she sometimes feels scared when her partner drinks alcohol.
She denies any physical harm but admits to feeling emotionally drained and isolated.
She has not had any postpartum complications and her infant is healthy.
She has no known drug allergies
Her vital signs are within normal limits
On examination, she appears fatigued but is otherwise well-appearing. and her physical exam is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: No menstrual period for the past 6 months while breastfeeding 8-month-old infant

lines: No menstrual period for the past 6 months while breastfeeding 8-month-old infant
The patient returns for evaluation of amenorrhea with a history of postpartum depression and thyroiditis, as well as prior lactational mastitis.
She reports that she has been exclusively breastfeeding her 8-month-old infant since birth.
She is not using any form of contraception and is not sexually active since the birth of her child.
She denies any hot flashes, vaginal dryness, or changes in libido.
Her body mass index is within the normal range.

encounters.cc: Persistent fever and lower abdominal pain five days after cesarean section

lines: Persistent fever and lower abdominal pain five days after cesarean section
This 35-year-old with postpartum thyroiditis and prior mastitis presents with fever and lower abdominal pain.
She gave birth to a healthy infant via cesarean section 10 days ago.
Her postoperative course was complicated by endometritis, for which she has been receiving intravenous antibiotics.
Despite this treatment, her fever has not resolved.
She reports no cough, dysuria, or diarrhea.
On examination, her temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), heart rate is 110/min, and blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg.
Abdominal examination reveals lower quadrant tenderness without rebound or guarding.
Pelvic examination is significant for tenderness over the uterine fundus and adnexal regions bilaterally.
A pelvic ultrasound shows no evidence of abscess.

encounters.cc: Routine postpartum visit with persistent sadness, fatigue, and difficulty sleeping

lines: Routine postpartum visit with persistent sadness, fatigue, and difficulty sleeping

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a history of postpartum depression and postpartum thyroiditis who returns for routine postpartum psychiatric care following recent recovery from puerperal septic thrombophlebitis.
She gave birth to a healthy baby girl 6 weeks ago.
She reports feeling persistently sad, fatigued, and overwhelmed since the delivery.
She has difficulty sleeping, even when her baby is asleep, and has lost interest in activities she used to enjoy, including caring for her newborn.
She expresses guilt about not being a good mother and has had thoughts of harming herself.
Her appetite has decreased significantly, and she has lost 10 pounds since the delivery.
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
On physical examination, she appears tired but is otherwise unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of fever, malaise, and left breast pain while breastfeeding

lines: Two-day history of fever, malaise, and left breast pain while breastfeeding
The patient is a 35-year-old female with a history of postpartum depression and prior lactational mastitis who presents with recurrent symptoms.
She is currently breastfeeding her 2-month-old infant and reports that the symptoms began shortly after she started using a new breastfeeding technique.
On examination, there is a localized area of erythema and induration on the upper outer quadrant of her left breast.
There is also tenderness to palpation in the same area and enlarged, tender left axillary lymph nodes.
The rest of the examination is unremarkable.
Her complete blood count shows a mild leukocytosis.

encounters.cc: Routine check-up regarding absence of menstrual periods for six months with IUD in place

lines: Routine check-up regarding absence of menstrual periods for six months with IUD in place
The patient returns for routine follow-up with history of postpartum thyroiditis, postpartum depression, and prior lactational amenorrhea in 2022.
She recently delivered via cesarean section in April 2023.
She reports that her menstrual periods have become progressively lighter since the IUD was inserted and she has not had a period for the last 6 months.
She denies any vaginal bleeding, discharge, or pelvic pain.
She inquires about the absence of her menstrual periods and whether this is a cause for concern.
She is currently using a levonorgestrel intrauterine device (IUD) for contraception, which was placed 2 years ago, and she is not taking any other medications
Her vital signs are within normal limits
Her abdominal and pelvic examinations are unremarkable
She is not anemic and her thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level is within the normal range.
Her recent Pap smear was normal.
